title: Random forest screens childhood DNA methylation sites linked to later BMI change
summary: In 325 children of the Isle of Wight birth cohort, recursive random forest screened genome-wide CpG sites for association with the change in BMI status from pre- to post-adolescence. Of 174 candidate CpGs, pre-adolescent methylation at 38 was associated with BMI transition, 30 of them gender-specific. Thirteen CpGs (11 gender-specific) showed consistent associations in the independent ALSPAC cohort. This is an association, not causation, and the random forest serves as a screening step before logistic regression.
ai_technology: Recursive random forest screening of CpG sites

evidence.tested: Replication in the independent ALSPAC cohort: 13 consistent CpGs.
evidence.unknown: Causality; the replication cohort size is not stated in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Recursive random forest screened genome-wide methylation data for candidate sites.
